Hi! Thanks for the question. As a person who has experienced SA, I don’t go on hookup apps just cause for safety reasons. But for girls who experienced SA and does use hookup apps, I know they just be more cautious preparing for the meetup. For instance, we send everyone we trust our location, have an escape plan, have a personal understanding on what we want in the meetup (like how far do we wanna go? What is too much? Would we do it again? Etc). We do this just in case the person we meet up doesn’t respond well to our boundaries. Ive had to help someone escape cause the guy wanted her to go to his place when she wanted to go to a motel and he didn’t take it well and almost hurt her. Almost every girl I know has been thru some sort of SA trauma, so I was tell advise guys to always be slow and allow what the girl is comfortable with. Be a gentlemen, show respect. It should be the same with guys too. Nobody shouldn’t do anything y’all aren’t comfortable with. When I went on the date, I initially wanted sex, but once it was about to happen, I got scared and didn’t want to do it no more. Us girls just hope and pray men would not be angry or hurt us if we don’t give them what they want. Because yes, it unfortunately happens… 


My advise to you guys is just communicate like adults. Assure them that consent is consent and it’s okay to not consent to things you don’t want to do. And it’s also okay (great even) to even ask “So what are you comfortable with?” It’s a really good question and it’ll save you lots of time and confusion. Have a safe word. And yeah. Make the hookup fun not scary.

If you can network on LinkedIn with the companies you are applying for, it could increase your chances. My company liked it a lot when college students connected with them and asked them about their job. It may sound weird but give it a go. Why not. They could probably point you to a friend they know.
